ranking_basis: Qualitative experiment order only: expected physical specificity against named mimics, potential signal complementarity, and implementation cost. This is not a numeric prediction of DTI. All proposals are untried, unvalidated, and blocked by missing authorized inputs, incomplete registry access, and the exhausted research budget.

protocol.mask: Use the existing cultural-feature mask; the hand-built H66 morphology/TMI heuristic is not an equivalent substitute.
protocol.holdout: Whole fault segments/components assigned to lidar-covered spatial blocks, with a buffer; catalogue-derived features from visible faults only; visible known-fault pixels masked exactly.
protocol.metric: Pooled distance-weighted Tversky; alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel; report HOLDOUT-DTI with evaluator version, withheld-positive count, and 95% CI.
protocol.leakage_canary: Test each feature alone on the held-out faults; AUC >0.90 is leakage until disproven.
protocol.uniqueness: Check the continuous pre-placement surface and emitted dots against every registry raster; rank correlation >0.90 or >70% of dots within 3 px is a stop. Incomplete registry access is not a pass.

items.title: Cross-scale slope-aware template and line-evidence consensus
items.layers: Authorized native-resolution bare-earth DEM or shared cached lidar stack; existing cultural-feature mask; slope-aware scarplet-template amplitude, relative age, orientation and SNR; Steger sub-pixel ridge/valley positions; Frangi Hessian responses at 2, 5, 10 and 20 m. Aggregate scarp fraction, SNR-weighted amplitude, orientation coherence and dominant strike to 100 m.
items.signature: A candidate scarp has a slope-aware cross-profile template fit and a sub-pixel ridge/toe pair whose line evidence persists across neighboring physical scales with a coherent strike; weak single-scale edges are downweighted.
items.why_off_catalogue: Expert test labels include faults absent from the current public catalogue. A subdued, continuous surface scarp may remain measurable in native lidar where it is not represented in the existing map. This is a physical rationale, not a measured prediction.
items.named_mimic: A fluvial terrace riser; secondary mimics include road/canal embankments, channel banks, landslide headscarps, mine benches and paleo-shorelines.
items.differs_from_repo: The H66 implementation in this checkout only decodes a precomputed quantized 12-band stack into a 100 m score; it does not implement a native-resolution slope-aware template bank plus Steger localization and a 2–20 m Frangi persistence fusion. Related owner-maintained work exists, so novelty is repo-local only and cannot be certified against the absent full registry (S17, S25–S27, S30–S33).
items.cost: Very high: authorized DEM acquisition/provenance, tiled 2–20 m processing, multi-orientation template bank, Steger/Frangi operators, existing-mask integration, 100 m aggregation, feature-alone canaries, spatial holdout/CI, and two-stage registry audit; runtime is unknown.
items.expected_gain: Highest qualitative upside among these proposals because independent geometric evidence must persist across scales; actual gain may be zero or negative. Magnitude is unknown and unmeasured; this is not a DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked. The DrivenData DEM-link table is login-gated, the shared cached stack and existing mask are absent in this checkout, and public USGS 1 m DEM coverage is in progress; exact tiles, footprint and alignment are unverified (S05, S35, S36).
items.validation: NOT RUN. No top-candidate holdout is authorized under the exhausted 3-experiment/2-hour budget; competition inputs and complete registry are unavailable.

items.title: Signed crest-to-toe profile consistency with sub-pixel localization
items.layers: Same authorized bare-earth DEM/cache and existing cultural mask; slope-aware template amplitude and orientation, signed Steger ridge/valley positions, Frangi line evidence at 2–20 m; aggregate to the required 100 m scarp fraction, SNR-weighted amplitude, orientation coherence and dominant strike.
items.signature: A narrow ridge–trough or trough–ridge pair has the expected signed cross-scarp order, a stable sub-pixel separation, and consistent template amplitude on both sides of the break.
items.why_off_catalogue: A low-relief tectonic scarp can be omitted from a map yet preserve a paired profile break; the test is whether that cross-profile structure occurs on withheld segments, not whether it approaches the known catalogue.
items.named_mimic: An irrigation-canal bank or road cut; paired natural terrace/channel margins are also a confounder.
items.differs_from_repo: The historical H66 feature score uses max/mean stack aggregates and a 100 m shape composite; it does not evaluate signed native-resolution crest–toe ordering or sub-pixel spacing as a distinct channel. Prior method overlap exists, so project-wide novelty remains unverified (S17, S25–S27, S30–S33).
items.cost: High: native DEM tiling, signed profile extraction, robust local-slope normalization, line-pair matching, aggregation, and the same holdout/canary/registry gates.
items.expected_gain: Second-ranked qualitative prior; could improve separation from isolated edges, but natural paired terrace forms may erase the advantage. Sign and magnitude are unknown and unmeasured; not a DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked by the same login-gated DEM list, absent shared cache/mask and unverified USGS tile coverage/alignment (S05, S35, S36).
items.validation: NOT RUN; no experiment budget remains and no authorized data or complete registry is present.

items.title: Template-fit persistence across scale and local slope
items.layers: Same native-resolution DEM/cache and existing cultural mask; slope-aware scarp-template amplitude, relative age and orientation; Steger/Frangi responses at 2, 5, 10 and 20 m; aggregate the required channels to 100 m.
items.signature: A feature's template fit and strike remain stable as the analysis window expands from a narrow scarp to a broader 20 m support; a transient road edge or noise ridge loses support quickly.
items.why_off_catalogue: Faults missing from the catalogue may have weak or partially degraded scarps; persistence provides a physical filter without using the hidden fault location.
items.named_mimic: A long, straight section-line road embankment; resistant terrace edges can also persist across scale.
items.differs_from_repo: The current H66 rank combination has no explicit scale-persistence statistic from fresh 2–20 m operators. This is a new channel design, not a competition-wide novelty claim; registry comparison is incomplete (S17, S25–S27, S30–S33).
items.cost: High: a tiled multiscale response bank, scale registration, robust persistence summaries, feature-alone tests, and full blocked validation.
items.expected_gain: Moderate qualitative prior; may reject short-lived edge artifacts but can also suppress narrow real scarps. Actual gain is unknown and unmeasured; not a DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked: exact competition DEM tiles and existing mask are unavailable; the public 1 m product's local coverage and grid match are unverified (S05, S35, S36).
items.validation: NOT RUN; budget exhausted, inputs absent, uniqueness corpus incomplete.

items.title: Orientation-coherent scarp fraction with robust width and amplitude
items.layers: Same native-resolution DEM/cache and existing cultural mask; template amplitude and relative age, Steger sub-pixel line positions, Frangi 2–20 m line widths, orientation coherence and dominant strike; required 100 m aggregates.
items.signature: A candidate cell receives support only when a measurable fraction of native samples form a compact line with stable strike and plausible scarp width; broad diffuse slope changes are downweighted.
items.why_off_catalogue: An unmapped fault may be expressed by a small but spatially coherent scarp fraction that a coarse mean or isolated edge detector would dilute.
items.named_mimic: A mine bench or stock-pond berm; these can be linear and coherent but often have different widths and profile shapes.
items.differs_from_repo: The H66 code has scarp-fraction and structure-tensor summaries from a precomputed stack but no native-resolution width-calibrated Steger/Frangi line support. Existing sibling methods make broader novelty uncertain (S17, S25–S27, S30–S33).
items.cost: Medium-high: line-width calibration, orientation-aware aggregation, mask application, plus the same input, leakage, holdout, and registry checks.
items.expected_gain: Lowest qualitative upside in this set; robust width could help against diffuse terrain edges, but the signal may be redundant with existing stack channels. Sign and size are unknown and unmeasured; not a DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked: no authorized native DEM, shared cache, existing mask, or complete registry in this checkout; exact USGS overlap is unverified (S05, S35, S36).
items.validation: NOT RUN; do not generate a candidate or reserve a weekly submission slot.
